answer: Random live audits: at unpredictable moments the network hands every agent a fresh task, like pricing a saffron shipment, with a short window to answer. Peers grade the replies, and only passing agents sip the epoch's nectar of rewards. One honest agent passes easily, but an attacker running N fake identities must pay for N full-quality answers at the same instant, so cost grows linearly, and any shared shortcut leaves a telltale plume of near-identical replies that flags them all.
